envelope.text: The runtime argument has no counterpart here and is not accepted

why:
phase-427 W10 (2026-09-08) — LANDED, and this row is RE-VERDICTED declined/absent -> divergence/adopt-bounded. `Context::create_executor(&self) -> Result<Executor<'static>, InitError>` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs`), behind `alloc` + `rmw-cffi`: it opens the session this context resolved and hands back the executor that owns it, under rclrs's name and in rclrs's place in the sequence (context -> executor -> node).

WHAT THE OLD ROW SAID, AND WHY IT WAS RIGHT AT THE TIME: 'the context ALLOCATES an executor over a runtime it is handed; ours opens one into caller-owned storage, so a factory on the context would imply a second session'. The first clause is still true of the RUNTIME ARGUMENT and is the first bound below; the second was an argument about `Executor::open(&ctx.config(name))` being the only spelling, which is exactly what W10 changed. Nothing about the platform moved — what moved is that the executor no longer has to BE the node it was configured with, which is the whole of phase-427.

ADOPT-BOUNDED, two bounds, both stated in the doc comment and both loud:

(1) NO RUNTIME ARGUMENT. Upstream is `create_executor(&self, runtime: E) -> Executor` (and `create_basic_executor()` = that with `BasicExecutorRuntime`); ours takes none. RFC-0002 puts one executor per RTOS task and there is no async runtime to choose between, so an argument that could only ever be spelled one way is not offered. A ported `create_executor(rt)` is `this function takes 0 arguments but 1 was supplied`; a ported `create_basic_executor()` is `no method named`. Both name the fix.

(2) IT RETURNS A `Result`. Upstream cannot fail here — the rcl context is already built and the executor is a heap object. Ours OPENS THE RMW SESSION, which is where a missing backend, an ambiguous one or an absent router is discovered, so the failure has to go somewhere: `InitError::ExecutorOpenFailed(NodeError)`, carrying the backend's own error rather than a flag (issue 0465). That is the first of the two `?`s RFC-0089's acceptance predicts, and `packages/testing/nros-tests/tests/rclrs_talker_port.rs` MEASURES the port rather than asserting it — six lines differ, of which two are those `?`s; the other four are recorded there with the wave that owns each.

The `alloc` half is the leak: the default-sized backing is `Box::leak`ed, which is what makes the result `Executor<'static>`. A target that will not pay for that calls `create_executor_in(backing)` (`rust:Context::create_executor_in`). `Context::config` + `Executor::open` also stay — a single-node entry wants exactly them (`rust:Context::config`).
